article_title: Microsoft and Chevron Plan a 2.67-Gigawatt Gas Plant to Directly Power a West Texas AI Data Center

content_preview.title: Microsoft and Chevron Plan a 2.67-Gigawatt Gas Plant to Directly Power a West Texas AI Data Center
content_preview.summary: Microsoft and Chevron unveiled Project Kilby, a co-located 2.67-gigawatt natural gas plant in West Texas that will supply a Microsoft AI and cloud data center under a 20-year power agreement.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Microsoft and Chevron announced plans on Monday to develop a 2.67-gigawatt natural gas power plant in West Texas to serve the tech company's AI and cloud data centers, [according to TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/22/microsoft-and-chevron-plan-one-of-the-largest-gas-powered-data-center-projects-in-us/). Microsoft will buy power from the plant, known as Project Kilby, for 20 years, [TechCrunch reported](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/22/microsoft-and-chevron-plan-one-of-th...

editor_notes.content_quality: Tight, well-structured News piece (496 words, within the 400-1200 News range). Clear Overview / What We Know / Why It Matters / What We Don't Know sections. Deliberately conservative sourcing: the Journalist restricted the article to two allowlisted outlets and openly delineates the limits of what those sources establish.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both source snapshots from disk (both status 200, sha256 verified against manifest). source-0.html.gz (TechCrunch, 'Microsoft and Chevron plan one of the largest gas-powered data center projects in US', Tim De Chant, posted 1:37 PM PDT June 22, 2026 / Monday): confirms verbatim the 2.67-GW figure, West Texas location, Microsoft+Chevron parties, 20-year power purchase agreement, the 'Project Kilby' name, the 'among the largest co-located natural gas power and data center developments in the U.S.' Chevron press-release quote, GE Vernova turbines + Solar Turbines (a Caterpillar subsidiary), the Environmental Integrity Project emissions estimate (>13M tons CO2, 3,200 tons criteria air pollutants, 278,000 lbs hazardous air pollutants), and Microsoft's 2030 carbon-elimination pledge. source-1.html.gz (Utility Dive, 'Data center activity exploded in Texas, spiking reliability risks: monitor', Robert Walton, July 14 2025): confirms 'exploded', the 70.5 GW of new load interconnectable to the ERCOT system by 2028, the Texas RE 'disorganized integration of large loads constitutes the largest increased risk' conclusion, and the 'very fast, very large ramps' quote attributed to David Penny. Both body source URLs appear in article.sources (no orphan citation; no bidirectional gap).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific, quote, name, number and date traces to one of the two cited snapshots. All direct quotes appear verbatim in the snapshots. The article faithfully paraphrases TechCrunch's turbine description as 'large GE Vernova turbines' without asserting a turbine count, correctly sidestepping the count discrepancy (TechCrunch says 'two'; other non-allowlisted outlets reported 'seven'). Verified that no specifics sourced only to bot-blocked/non-allowlisted outlets leaked into the body: no Permian sourcing, no Reeves County/Pecos location, no FID timing, no first-power 2028, no ~$10B tax figure, no ~2,000 jobs, no Engine No.1, no Gustavson quote. The one '2028' in the body is the properly sourced Utility Dive ERCOT load-forecast year, not a plant commissioning date. The 'What We Don't Know' section transparently flags the absence of cost, commissioning date, phasing, grid-connection terms, and permit-based emissions.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. The climate tension is presented factually ('sits awkwardly against Microsoft's climate commitments') and attributed to TechCrunch's framing.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No existing article covers Project Kilby or the Microsoft-Chevron West Texas gas plant. Adjacent July 2026 data-center coverage (Digital Realty Kansas campus, Microsoft hollow-core fiber) concerns unrelated events. No duplication.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean APPROVE. A disciplined, source-conservative News brief in which every load-bearing claim is verified against a cited, snapshotted source; no fabrication, no orphaned citation, no leakage of non-allowlisted specifics.
